item.title: Police defend operations, claiming serious crime rates have decreased
item.description: The Fiji Police Force says serious crime rates have declined this year despite recent public criticism over aggravated robberies and burglaries, with Police Commissioner Rusiate Tudravu calling for a nationwide approach to tackling the causes of crime. Mr Tudravu said Police accepted criticism of its operations following several high-profile incidents and was adjusting strategies to ensure respons
item.content:encoded:
The Fiji Police Force says serious crime rates have declined this year despite recent public criticism over aggravated robberies and burglaries, with Police Commissioner Rusiate Tudravu calling for a nationwide approach to tackling the causes of crime.

Mr Tudravu said Police accepted criticism of its operations following several high-profile incidents and was adjusting strategies to ensure responses were proactive rather than reactive.

Police statistics for January to July 2026 show burglary declined by 7.3 per cent, robbery by 32.8 per cent, aggravated robbery by 17.8 per cent, aggravated burglary by 7.7 per cent and theft by 7.9 per cent compared with the same period last year.

However, motor vehicle theft increased from 31 cases during the first seven months of 2025 to 51 this year.

Overall crime declined by 11 per cent, from 11,387 cases in January-July 2025 to 10,106 during the corresponding period this year.

“The posture and strategies adopted by operations for the first six months has resulted in the reduction in these crimes,” Mr Tudravu said.

He acknowledged the figures could be met with scepticism amid recent cases attracting significant public attention.

“While this will be met with scepticism, the Fiji Police Force accepts constructive criticism to avoid predictable policing patterns that may be exploited by offenders,” he said.

Mr Tudravu said arrests alone would not provide a lasting solution and called for greater attention to why people repeatedly committed crimes.

“The why factor. This is where we need to also focus our attention as a nation,” he said.

“We have individuals coming into the system who are habitual offenders with multiple theft or burglary cases, which begs two critical questions, why and what can be an effective deterrent?”

Mr Tudravu also acknowledged the value of CCTV footage in investigations but rejected suggestions Police only responded after videos appeared on social media.

He called for discussions on stronger deterrents and alternatives for people who had developed what he described as a worrying reliance on crime to earn a living.

“Crime prevention is everyone’s responsibility,” Mr Tudravu said.

item.title: Online safety laws under review
item.description: FIJI’s legal framework for dealing with cyber harm is being reviewed as the country responds to the growing challenges created by an increasingly digital society. Justice Minister and Acting Attorney-General Siromi Turaga told Parliament on Wednesday last week that the Fiji Law Reform Commission was advancing its review of the Online Safety Act 2018.
item.content:encoded:
FIJI’s legal framework for dealing with cyber harm is being reviewed as the country responds to the growing challenges created by an increasingly digital society.

Justice Minister and Acting Attorney-General Siromi Turaga told Parliament on Wednesday last week that the Fiji Law Reform Commission was advancing its review of the Online Safety Act 2018.

The review has recently completed its final validation workshop, allowing stakeholders to provide feedback on an interim final report and draft Bill.

Mr Turaga said the review was aimed at strengthening Fiji’s legal response to harmful activity online.

“Its objective is very clear – to strengthen Fiji’s legal framework to better address cyber harm and challenges created by the increase in digital society,” he said.

“The final package is now being prepared for handover to my office this month.”

The review is one of several major law reform projects being undertaken by the commission, which also included the Mining Act 1965, Quarries Act, Security Industry Act 2010, Human Trafficking Laws and court rules.

Mr Turaga said the commission’s work reflected the need for laws to keep pace with technological and social change.

“Law reform is not simply about changing legislation for the sake of change – it is about asking more important questions.

“Are our laws still serving the people, the institutions and society they were created to serve?”

He said consultation remained a critical part of the process, with the people affected by legislation needing an opportunity to understand, question and contribute to its development.

“Good laws cannot be developed in isolation from the people who live under them.”

item.title: Hospital bed upgrade rolls out
item.description: Fiji’s health system is set for a major infrastructure boost, with the Ministry of Health rolling out 1502 new medical furniture and equipment units as part of a multi-year hospital bed upgrade program. Health and Medical Services Minister Dr Atonio Lalabalavu told Parliament that around 400 modern general hospital beds are expected to be delivered during the first phase of the program this financ
item.content:encoded:
Fiji’s health system is set for a major infrastructure boost, with the Ministry of Health rolling out 1502 new medical furniture and equipment units as part of a multi-year hospital bed upgrade program.

Health and Medical Services Minister Dr Atonio Lalabalavu told Parliament that around 400 modern general hospital beds are expected to be delivered during the first phase of the program this financial year, targeting facilities facing the greatest pressure.

The Western Division will receive 84 beds for Nadi Hospital, 74 for Sigatoka Hospital, 43 for Rakiraki Hospital and 29 for Tavua Hospital. Labasa Hospital will receive specialised electric beds for its Coronary Care Unit and operating theatres, while Colonial War Memorial Hospital will receive new beds for several critical wards, including children’s, labour, postnatal, birthing and intensive care units.

Tamavua Twomey Hospital will also receive 39 beds for its Dermatology and Tuberculosis Ward.

The broader tender includes 779 general beds allocated across the divisions, along with specialised paediatric, psychiatric, cardiac and emergency beds, patient trolleys, electric examination couches, stretchers and wheelchairs.

Dr Lalabalavu said the three-year rollout would allow equipment to be properly inspected, installed and maintained while replacing ageing and unsafe equipment in facilities nationwide.

item.title: BE-GREEN to support 3050 rural households – Tunabuna
item.description: A NEW program is set to support thousands of rural households in Vanua Levu, with the Government promising stronger farming systems, healthier fishing grounds, ecosystem restoration and new economic opportunities. Minister for Agriculture and Waterways Tomasi Tunabuna told Parliament on Wednesday last week that the Blue Economy and Green Community Development Programme (BE-GREEN) was officially la
item.content:encoded:
A NEW program is set to support thousands of rural households in Vanua Levu, with the Government promising stronger farming systems, healthier fishing grounds, ecosystem restoration and new economic opportunities.

Minister for Agriculture and Waterways Tomasi Tunabuna told Parliament on Wednesday last week that the Blue Economy and Green Community Development Programme (BE-GREEN) was officially launched by Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka on July 24 in Koronatoga Village, Cakaudrove.

“This landmark initiative reflects the Coalition Government’s unwavering commitment to safeguarding Fiji’s natural resources while creating sustainable economic opportunities for our rural communities,” Mr Tunabuna said.

The program, supported by the International Fund for Agricultural Development and the Global Environment Facility, will cover six Cakaudrove districts – Eastern Wailevu, Savusavu, Navatu, Koroalau, Vaturova and Naweni.

About 3050 subsistence and semi-commercial farming, fishing and handicraft-producing households are expected to benefit.

Mr Tunabuna said BE-GREEN would focus on boosting rural incomes, restoring ecosystems and strengthening communities against climate change and environmental degradation.

“The program has been designed to strengthen the productive capacity of Vanua Levu agriculture and marine sector through sustainable resource management, biodiversity enhancing practices, and climate smart approaches development.”

Opposition Leader Inia Seruiratu backed the initiative but called for stronger implementation, monitoring and coordination.

He said women and youth participation were critical to tackling rural-urban migration.

“This is how we can create employment in the rural areas, and most importantly, empower them economically as well,” Mr Seruiratu said.

He also urged greater focus on agroforestry, reforestation, organic fertilisers and renewable energy.

item.title: Mother’s loss inspires Latianara
item.description: FOR 20-year-old Suliana Ilisabeta Latianara, the loss of her mother has become a source of strength and a powerful motivation to advocate for young women. The eldest of eight siblings from Nacamaki Village on Koro, Lomaiviti, Ms Latianara also has maternal links to Baravi and Navakasiga in Bua.
item.content:encoded:
FOR 20-year-old Suliana Ilisabeta Latianara, the loss of her mother has become a source of strength and a powerful motivation to advocate for young women.

The eldest of eight siblings from Nacamaki Village on Koro, Lomaiviti, Ms Latianara also has maternal links to Baravi and Navakasiga in Bua.

Last year, she lost her mother to cancer. Since then, she has taken on greater responsibilities at home while continuing to balance her studies, work and community commitments.

A journalism student and former Teen Duavata titleholder, Suliana says her passion lies in connecting with people, amplifying voices and celebrating Fiji’s diversity.

“Losing my mum was the hardest thing but I had to step up,” she said.

“My siblings, my dad, my community — they need me. It’s not easy balancing everything, but I keep going.”

Despite the weight of responsibility, she remains committed to completing her studies and serving her community. Ms Latianara sees her experience as an opportunity to encourage other young women facing difficult circumstances.

“My story is about resilience. If I can show other young women that you can keep going through grief and still chase your dreams, then I’ve done something right.”

item.title: Minister condemns attack
item.description: PUBLIC service vehicle drivers should not have to risk their safety or livelihoods while carrying out their work, says Transport Minister Ro Filipe Tuisawau. “Public Service Vehicle (PSV) drivers provide an essential public transport service and should not have to put their lives and livelihoods at risk while doing their jobs.”
item.content:encoded:
PUBLIC service vehicle drivers should not have to risk their safety or livelihoods while carrying out their work, says Transport Minister Ro Filipe Tuisawau.

“Public Service Vehicle (PSV) drivers provide an essential public transport service and should not have to put their lives and livelihoods at risk while doing their jobs.”

Ro Filipe said PSV drivers worked hard to earn a living while providing an essential service and should be able to do their jobs without fear.

He said he was concerned by the circumstances surrounding the recent incident in Nadi.

While respecting the ongoing police investigation, Ro Filipe called on members of the public to refrain from violence, intimidation and other criminal behaviour towards taxidrivers and other public transport providers.

Meanwhile, two more suspects are in custody as police continue their investigation into a viral video showing an aggravated robbery involving a taxidriver in Nadi.

Police confirmed the investigations were continuing to locate others who may have been involved in the alleged incident.

“The Western Division Taskforce continues to hunt for the fourth suspect whose identity is known to police,” they said.

Police had initially confirmed on Tuesday that a 23-year-old man had surrendered to police and was being questioned at the Lautoka Police Station.

item.title: Duo walk free | FICAC drops charges against former FBC executives
item.description: FORMER Fiji Broadcasting Corporation (FBC) chief executive officer Riyaz Sayed-Khaiyum has expressed relief that good sense ultimately prevailed, while maintaining that abuse of office charges brought against him and FBC chief financial officer Vimlesh Sagar had been frivolous from the outset. The comments came after the Prosecution formally dropped all charges, with Prosecutor Setefano Komaibaba
item.content:encoded:
FORMER Fiji Broadcasting Corporation (FBC) chief executive officer Riyaz Sayed-Khaiyum has expressed relief that good sense ultimately prevailed, while maintaining that abuse of office charges brought against him and FBC chief financial officer Vimlesh Sagar had been frivolous from the outset.

The comments came after the Prosecution formally dropped all charges, with Prosecutor Setefano Komaibaba filing a nolle prosequi signed by acting FICAC Commissioner Lavi Rokoika just as the trial was set to open in the Suva Magistrate’s Court yesterday.

Mr Sayed-Khaiyum was charged with abuse of office for gain and an alternative count of general dishonesty causing a loss. He was accused of initiating five legal proceedings without board approval between July 2017 and January 2023, incurring costs of $138,813.37.

Mr Sagar was charged with general dishonesty for allegedly approving $15,075.88 in payments to a law firm without prior board authorisation.

Speaking outside court, Mr Sayed-Khaiyum stated that the two-year legal battle had caused severe emotional strain on his family.

“The whole thing has been quite ridiculous,” Mr Sayed-Khaiyum said.

“Unfortunately, it put my family, my children, my wife, my parents, through a lot of trauma and hurt. I’m just glad it’s over.

“I just hope that this sort of nonsense doesn’t reoccur for anyone.”

He criticised the prosecution as a waste of public resources and taxpayer money and said he hoped good sense would prevail in a related pending matter.

Mr Sagar also welcomed the outcome after enduring more than 900 days under legal scrutiny.

He maintained that both executives acted within their delegated authority and strictly adhered to high standards of corporate governance, ethics, and integrity throughout their tenure.

“As authorised officers, we know our delegations of authority”, he said.

“We work under corporate governance as well with the highest level of ethical and governance levels.”

He said he had more than 22 years of service and had consistently upheld integrity and good corporate practices.

The pair have a separate matter before another court, where they are charged in relation to the tender and procurement of a 3.0-litre Volkswagen Touareg valued at $207,470. The matter is set for trial from November 2 to 6.

item.title: Senior population tops 90,000
item.description: MORE than 90,000 Fijians are now aged 60 years and over, accounting for more than one in every 10 people in the country. Minister for Women, Children and Social Protection Sashi Kiran said the figure highlighted the growing importance of ensuring older persons remain included, protected and supported in national development.
item.content:encoded:
MORE than 90,000 Fijians are now aged 60 years and over, accounting for more than one in every 10 people in the country.

Minister for Women, Children and Social Protection Sashi Kiran said the figure highlighted the growing importance of ensuring older persons remain included, protected and supported in national development.

In a statement, Ms Kiran said Fiji’s national report on ageing must be evidence-based and reflect the lived experiences of older persons across the country.

“Our elders are not only part of our past,” Ms Kiran said.

“They are the foundation of our present and remain important to our future.”

Ms Kiran made the comments following the opening of the National Validation workshop on Fiji’s Voluntary National Survey for the Fifth Asia-Pacific Review and Appraisal of the Madrid International Plan of Action on Ageing.

The two-day workshop brings together Government representatives, the National Council for Older Persons, HART Homes, non-governmental organisations and civil society to review and strengthen the national survey ahead of its submission for the regional review in 2027.

The process will consider the experiences of older persons in urban, rural, maritime and island communities, including older women, persons with disabilities, caregivers and those who worked mainly in the informal sector.

Fiji’s Draft National Ageing Policy 2026–2035 identifies six priority areas, including social protection and financial security, health and aged care, transport and accessibility, digital inclusion, climate-resilient infrastructure and legal protection.

Government support includes the Social Pension Scheme, transport assistance, free general practitioner services and investment in aged-care facilities.
